messages.subject: SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat problems PeptideSequence
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I am trying to anlayse my phospho-data, but I already have issues in the importation from Spectronaut (v21.0) with SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat. I had no issues with the normal proteomic analysis and its uploading with SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat.

With running following code:
SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat(
  "20261002_PCF000732_phospho_RT_Report.tsv",
  annotation = "Phosphoproteomics metadata.csv",
  fasta_path = "UP000000589_10090.fasta",
  protein_input = "20261002_PCF000732_RT_Report.tsv",
  annotation_protein = "Proteomics metadata.csv",
  use_unmod_peptides = FALSE,
  intensity = "PeakArea",
  mod_id = "\\[Phospho \\(STY\\)\\]",
  fasta_protein_name = "uniprot_iso",
  remove_other_mods = TRUE,
  filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
  qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
  useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
  removeFewMeasurements = TRUE,
  removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
  summaryforMultipleRows = max,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_file_path = NULL
)
I always get the following error:
Error in `[.data.table`(data, , c(protein_name_col, unmod_pep_col, mod_pep_col), : columns not found: [PG.ProteinGroups, PeptideSequence, EG.PrecursorId]

However, Spectronaut does not have any columns for 'PeptideSequence', and I have loaded the PEP.StrippedSequence and EG.ModifiedSequence columns:
> colnames(phospho)  [1] "R.Condition" "R.FileName" "R.Replicate" [4] "PG.Genes" "PG.ProteinAccessions" "PG.ProteinGroups" [7] "PG.IsSingleHit" "PG.Qvalue" "PG.Quantity" [10] "PEP.GroupingKey" "PEP.IsProteotypic" "PEP.PeptidePosition" [13] "PEP.StrippedSequence" "PEP.Quantity" "EG.iRTPredicted" [16] "EG.IsDecoy" "EG.Library" "EG.PrecursorId" [19] "EG.ModifiedSequence" "EG.Qvalue" "EG.ProteinPTMLocations" [22] "EG.PTMPositions [Phospho (STY)]" "EG.PTMSites [Phospho (STY)]" "EG.PTMAssayProbability" [25] "EG.PTMLocalizationProbabilities" "FG.Charge" "FG.Id" [28] "FG.PrecMz" "FG.Quantity" "F.Charge" [31] "F.FrgIon" "F.FrgLossType" "F.FrgMz" [34] "F.FrgNum" "F.FrgType" "F.PredictedRelativeIntensity" [37] "F.ExcludedFromQuantification" "F.NormalizedPeakArea" "F.NormalizedPeakHeight" [40] "F.PeakArea" "F.PeakHeight"

I now just read the raw phospho tsv with data.table::fread, and have added a column 'PeptideSequence' based on the excisting column 'PEP.StrippedSequence'. This seems to work for the uploading, but I wanted to make sure that this would 1) not effect downstream analysis and 2) that you were aware this occurs.

Thank you!

Best
Ryan

messages.subject: Spectronaut/MSstats: should fragments of non-identified peptides contribute to protein abundance?
messages.subject_clean: Spectronaut/MSstats: should fragments of non-identified peptides contribute to protein abundance?
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats community,

I analyze Orbitrap Astral DIA data using Spectronaut and MSstats.

Protein abundance results differ substantially between Spectronaut and MStats, due to the "Precursor Filtering : Identified (Q-value)"  in the quatification settings of spectronaut.

When "Quantification Data Filtering" is not marked (as inteded by the MSStats Report (v.3.7.3) report scheme) , low-level MS2 signals that appear to be background can produce protein abundance estimates despite the absence of accepted identifications. Given the Astral’s high MS2 sensitivity, this seems particularly relevant.

Is this expected and desirable behavior, or should these signals be excluded before MSstats processing?

Should Spectronaut’s “Quantification Data Filtering” be enabled, and which settings (particularly Precursor Filtering etc.) would you recommend?

Thank you!

Adrian

messages.subject_clean: Spectronaut/MSstats: should fragments of non-identified peptides contribute to protein abundance?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

This is a real gap rather than a misconfiguration. SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat has a filter_with_Qvalue argument that defaults to FALSE, so by default MSstats applies no q-value cutoff at all. If Spectronaut's own quantification filtering is also off, nothing filters, which is most likely why your two sets of abundances diverge.

Set filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE and qvalue_cutoff = 0.01 to enable it. Note that the switch turns on filters for both EG.Qvalue and PG.Qvalue, though qvalue_cutoff sets the threshold for EG.Qvalue only; PG.Qvalue is fixed at 0.01.

Worth knowing it does not drop rows. It blanks the intensity and leaves the row in place, so MSstats treats the measurement as censored and imputes it rather than ignoring it. I would filter here rather than upstream in Spectronaut, since that keeps the full feature by run grid visible to MSstats.

Your point about the Astral is well taken, and I will raise internally whether the default should change.

Best,
Swaraj

messages.subject: Re: SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat problems PeptideSequence
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

Thanks for pointing this out.  I did an investigation and this looks like it's a misleading error message.  SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat should work as long as you have the column EG.PrecursorId or EG.ModifiedSequence (it looks like both of those columns exist for you).

I actually think the main issue is that the input for SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat needs to be a data.frame rather than a filename (so doing SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat(
    "20261002_PCF000732_phospho_RT_Report.tsv", .... ) doesn't work)

We'll first look to fix the misleading error message, then update the docs so that it's clear the input to the function is a dataframe.

Tony

messages.body_plain:
Hi Swaraj,

Thank you for the clarification and taking your time to consider my request. Especially, the helpful consideration that keeping Spectronauts filtering off and not deleting the rows, helps with imputation.

Still, one issue remains:

some of my precursors have EG.Qvalue < 0.01, but EG.Identified = FALSE, and Spectronaut reports no accepted protein identification in that run (PG.Qvalue (Run-Wise).
However, the experiment-wide PG.Qvalue is below 0.01, so filtering on EG.Qvalue and PG.Qvalue would still retain these intensities. (I think also EG.QValue is determined across all runs and not run specific)

Does the converter consider run-wise protein or EG confidence?

Would you recommend an additional filter using PG.Qvalue (Run-Wise) or EG.Identified, or is retaining these signals as observed intensities for protein abundance estimation intended behavior?

Best,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: Spectronaut/MSstats: should fragments of non-identified peptides contribute to protein abundance?
messages.subject_clean: Spectronaut/MSstats: should fragments of non-identified peptides contribute to protein abundance?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

Good question. We looked at it internally and the answer is no on both counts.

EG.Identified reflects the cutoff you set in Spectronaut's own interface rather than an independent measure, so it is not something the converter can reason about. The
q-value columns are the meaningful input.

On run-wise PG.Qvalue, we are not filtering on it. Protein-group q-value estimation is still an open problem and the metric is not considered reliable enough to filter on by default. EG.Qvalue is calculated more soundly, which is why the precursor-level filter is the one we lean on. If you want the run-wise PG filter for your own analysis it is straightforward to apply to the report before conversion.

So retaining those signals is intended, with the caveat that the filtering we do apply is at the precursor and experiment-wide protein level rather than run-wise.

Best,
Swaraj

Dear MSstats Community: This year we are piloting May Institute Essentials: a mini and super concise version of the original May Institute program, fully online. The discussions will cover the core concepts of MSstats for mass spectrometry, lead by the original developers of the tools. Expect tutorial lectures, live case, studies, and 1:1 office hours for extra discussion, brainstorm or debug.

Please mark your calendar, and share with anyone who may benefit or be interested. Register at https://vitek-lab.github.io/MIe-2026/ and please share widely

Sincerely
Olga Vitek
Raymond Bradford Bradstreet Professor
Director, Barnett Institute for Chemical and Biological Analysis
Khoury College of Computer Sciences
Northeastern University

messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats community,

I am analyzing DIA-NN 2.7.0 output with MSstats 4.18.1 (R 4.5.0) on a computing cluster. I convert the DIA-NN report with the following call:

input <- DIANNtoMSstatsFormat(input = input,
                              annotation = annot,
                              quantificationColumn = "auto",
                              MBR = TRUE,
                              use_log_file = FALSE)

In the MSstats output, I see proteins that are supported only by shared peptides, i.e. none of their peptides is unique to them. In the DIA-NN report, these peptides are flagged Proteotypic = 0. I had expected that proteins without any proteotypic peptide would not appear in the MSstats output.

Is this expectation correct? Specifically, does DIANNtoMSstatsFormat (with useUniquePeptide = TRUE) use the Proteotypic column of the DIA-NN report to exclude such peptides, or does it only filter on Protein.Group assignment? It seems that DIANN is showing only one ID in "Protein.Group" based on maximum parsimony, but "Protein.Ids" column and "Proteotypic" column clearly shows that identification is based on shared peptide.

Thank you very much for your help.
Best regards,
NIk.

> Hi Adrian,
>
> Good question. We looked at it internally and the answer is no on both counts.
>
> EG.Identified reflects the cutoff you set in Spectronaut's own interface rather than an independent measure, so it is not something the converter can reason about. The
> q-value columns are the meaningful input.
>
> On run-wise PG.Qvalue, we are not filtering on it. Protein-group q-value estimation is still an open problem and the metric is not considered reliable enough to filter on by default. EG.Qvalue is calculated more soundly, which is why the precursor-level filter is the one we lean on. If you want the run-wise PG filter for your own analysis it is straightforward to apply to the report before conversion.
>
> So retaining those signals is intended, with the caveat that the filtering we do apply is at the precursor and experiment-wide protein level rather than run-wise.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nik,

Your understanding is correct. useUniquePeptide = TRUE does not use the Proteotypic column. Instead, it looks at the protein-peptide pairs after conversion, counts how many different proteins each peptide is assigned to, and keeps only peptides assigned to one protein. So the filter uses the ProteinName column after conversion, not the original DIA-NN report.

The issue is that DIA-NN applies maximum parsimony and reports a single entry in Protein.Group. As a result, a peptide with Proteotypic = 0 can still appear to map to just one protein when the filter is applied. Its count is therefore one, so it passes the filter. This explains why you're seeing proteins supported only by shared peptides.

To get the result you expected, filter the DIA-NN report before conversion:

```

input <- input[input$Proteotypic == 1, ]

```

Then run DIANNtoMSstatsFormat as before.

Thanks for the clear write-up. We will look at whether the converter should read Proteotypic directly.

Best,
Swaraj
